messages:
Kim: dropping a few follow-ups from today's infra all-hands about SLOs, burst behaviour, and observability so we don't lose track.

Arun: thanks  First Q: are we changing any SLO thresholds when traffic is served from the burst pool vs dedicated?

Kim: yes  SLOs are tiered: dedicated pools keep standard p99 latency targets. burst-served requests have a relaxed p99 target (2x) and a separate availability metric. we'll document in SLO playbook.

Vera: does that mean alerts will fire differently depending on where requests served from? oncall needs clarity.

Kim: alerts will include a tag `served_via` and oncall rules will reference it. e.g., p99_high where served_via=burst triggers a lower-severity alert.

SRE_Ravi: can we get a compact alert payload so paging only happens for real incidents? something like `region|served_via|metric|value`.

Arun: yes please  reduced noise is key.

infra-bot: [config] SLO tagging change deployed by @Kim  change-id: 9912  link: https://redwood.internal/infra/changes/9912 :white_check_mark:

Vera: operational question: when we reroute to burst, do we keep telemetry (trace ids, logs) attached to original request so CS can debug?

Kim: we propagate trace and session headers. Trace id remains same and we add `x-rw-served-via: burst-region` header. logs will show both hop entries.

Product_Mel: product ask: can we expose a simple per-customer "burst-usage" boolean in the console so account teams can proactively see when customers hit burst?

Kim: yes  we can add a per-account alert and a daily tag in the usage export. will need a small frontend ticket.

SRE_Ravi: runbook ask: what do we recommend during sustained high-burst usage? escalate to capacity or throttle?

Kim: runbook: 1) check region buffer and burst pool utilization, 2) if burst >50% sustained for 15m -> open capacity request, 3) notify account teams and enable cost_protection if requested. I'll add this to the daily ops checklist.

Arun: curious about cross-region throttle policies  if a customer opts into `cost_protection`, do we prioritize cheaper regions even if higher latency?

Kim: yes  cost_protection prefers cheaper fallbacks but will only pick higher-latency region if latency budget isn't breached. customers can always set `fallback_policy` to strict to avoid cross-region.

infra-bot: [alert] burst-utilization spike in eu-west by 42%  reported at 2076543300.

Vera: saw that spike, pinging SRE_Ravi to confirm runbook steps.

SRE_Ravi: on it  verifying region buffers and contacting capacity. I'll post an update in #eng-oncall within 10m.

Product_Mel: action items: 1) add burst-usage flag to account exports, 2) small frontend ticket for console exposure.

Kim: ops action items: 1) update SLO playbook with burst SLOs and alert tags, 2) add compact alert payload format, 3) publish runbook note about sustained burst. tagging @SRE_Ravi and @Vera.

Arun: thanks  I'll follow up with a short note for sales on what burst means for customers.

Vera: :eyes:

SRE_Ravi: :raised_hands:
